claim_scope: BOTH, for the study cell only (receiver input stage; no channel model). This is study evidence for issue #386's candidate confirmation, not design evidence: the T-10 manifest row stays on the committed cell's failing record until an adoption lands.
study: issue #386 receiver-threshold sizing study; the candidate is the supply-referenced input stage (NMOS pair + PMOS mirror load against a matched rppd VDDIO/2 divider) selected by records/20261121T084734Z-screen/ and inlined in tb_mc.cir as aib_rx_data. design/aib_rx_data.spice is unchanged.
bench_deviations: The nominal bench is the committed T-10 request shape (sim/mc/request_t10.json: same 45-corner PVT-FULL mismatch grid, same DC sweep 0.3-0.7, same limits and target_sigma, seeds 4410/4411, control degradation = input-side NMOS 4x narrower). One deviation: the control bench widens its DC sweep to 0.15-0.95, because the degraded candidate crosses at fr 0.66-0.75 over the grid (outside the committed 0.3-0.7 window, measured at tt/1.200V/27C and sf/1.080V/-40C during the study's local probes); the nominal bench keeps the committed window.
note: T-10 PASSES for the study's supply-referenced candidate: pooled over the 45-corner grid the offset is +2.7 mV mean, 9.6 mV sigma (sigma-to-spec 5.96 against the 3 target); 0 of 5400 draws outside +-60 mV; the binding corner mean is +10.8 mV (ff/1.320V/125C, per_corner.md). Measured mismatch sigma (8.5-10.8 mV per corner) is about twice the screen's 1/sqrt(area) estimate from the inverter record -- the mirror load's mismatch adds -- but the candidate's mean span across corners is 12.7 mV against the inverter's 84.9 mV, which is what closes the row. Study evidence only: the spec row stays on the committed cell's failing record until the adoption issue lands.
